stem: The Planning Commission has been abolished by Prime Minister
expl: The Planning Commission was set up in March 1950 by the first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru to optimize scarce resources in newly-born Nation. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on August 15, 2014, from the Red Fort to abolish the old Planning Commission. In accordance with a key announcement made by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Independence Day, the Union Government established NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India), as a replacement for the Planning Commission on January 1, 2015. NITI Aayog will seek to provide a critical directional and strategic input into the developmental process.

stem: Who appoints the Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog?

options.label: d
options.text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

expl: On January 1, 2015, the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established as the successor to the Planning Commission. It is a non-constitutional or extra-constitutional body (i.e., not created by the Constitution) and a non-statutory body (not created by an Act of the Parliament). It was created by an executive resolution of the Government of India. The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairman of the NITI Aayog. A Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister. He enjoys the rank of a Cabinet Minister. Former World Bank economist, Suman Bery is the current vice-chairperson of the NITI Aayog. Dr. Arvind Pangariya served as the first vice-chairman of the NITI Aayog, from January, 2015 to August, 2017.

stem: When was the Planning Commission established?
expl: The Planning Commission was a non-Constitutional institution. It is not mentioned in the Constitution. The Commission was formed by a resolution of the Cabinet on March 15, 1950. Prime Minister used to be the ex-officio Chairman of this Commission. Its main function was to prepare a 5-year plan for the Union and to give suggestions on the annual plans of the States. Almost 70 percent of grants to the States by the Centre were given on the recommendation of the Commission. NITI Aayog has replaced the Planning Commission. It is also an extra-Constitutional body. It was formed by a resolution of the Union Cabinet on 1 January, 2015.

Which of the following body/bodies does not/do not find mention in the Constitution?
1. National Development Council
2. Planning Commission
3. Zonal Councils
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
expl: The National Development Council, the Planning Commission, and the Zonal Councils are not mentioned in the Constitution of India. These are extra-Constitutional bodies established by executive order. The National Development Council and the Planning Commission were established in 1952 and 1950, respectively, and the Zonal Councils are statutory bodies constituted under the State Reorganisation Act, 1956.

stem: Which one of the following is not correct about NITI Aayog?

options.label: c
options.text: It was set up in January 2015

options.label: d
options.text: It is based on the principle of Cooperative Federalism

expl: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India Aayog) is a Government of India policy think-tank, which came into being on 1 January, 2015 to replace the Planning Commission (Yojna Aayog). Like the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog is an extra-Constitutional body. This Aayog works on the principle of Co-operative federalism. Code :

stem: Which one of the following statements in not true?

options.label: a

options.label: c
options.text: Secretary of the Planning Commission is also the Secretary of the National Development Council.

options.label: d
options.text: The National Development Council is presided over by the Prime Minister of India.

expl: The National Development Council (NDC) is the apex body for decision-making and deliberation on development matters in India. It is presided over by the Prime Minister. It is comprised of the Prime Minister as the Chairman of the Commission, Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog), Chief Ministers, Cabinet Ministers and the Members of the Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog). The other 3 options are true.

stem:
The National Development Council (NDC) –
1. Discusses the progress of the National Plan.
2. Suggests the ways to achieve the goals of the National Plan.
3. Gives guidelines to formulate the National Plan.
4. Suggests allocation of money in Planning.
Considering the above statements, select the correct answer from the code given below :
Codes :
expl: The National Development Council (NDC) was set up on 6 August, 1952 by an executive order of the Government. Its main functions are: (a) To prescribe guidelines for the formulation of the National Plan, including the assessment of resources for the plan; (b) To consider the National Plan as formulated by the Planning Commission; (c) To consider important questions of social and economic policy affecting National development; (d) To review the working of the Plan from time to time and to recommend such measures that are necessary for achieving the aims and targets set out in the National Plan. The Planning Commission suggested ways for the allocation of money to the National Plan, not the National Development Council.

expl: To ensure the participation of States in the formation of five-year plans, the National Development Council (NDC) was set up on 6 August, 1952 by an executive order of the Government. The Prime Minister is the Chairman of the National Development Council and all the Chief Ministers of the States are its members. The Secretary of the Planning Commission (now, NITI Aayog) is also the Ex-officio Secretary of the National Development Council. NDC finally approves five-year plans. NDC acts as a coordinator between the Planning Commission (now, NITI Aayog) and State Governments.
